skill.name: music-generation
skill.description: Compose, analyze, transform, render, and validate instrumental music using MIDI, music21, FluidSynth, and built-in electronic synthesis tools.
skill.summary: Generate original instrumental music and convert MIDI structures into downloadable audio.
skill.author: Cam10001110101

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences, MIDI terminology, static imports, documentation links, and expected output writes. Three static findings are confirmed: the installer changes host packages, and the renderer can delete existing sibling MIDI and WAV files. No prompt injection, credential access, covert networking, or exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Predictable cleanup paths can delete existing MIDI or WAV files.
remediation.suggestion: Create temporary files with tempfile, track ownership, and delete only files created by the current render operation.

remediation.issue: The installer changes system packages and upgrades pip automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, use a virtual environment, and separate optional operating-system installation from Python setup.

remediation.issue: Python dependencies use open-ended minimum versions.
remediation.suggestion: Publish tested upper bounds or a lock file with hashes to reduce dependency drift and supply-chain exposure.

content.user_title: Generate Original MIDI and Audio Music
content.value_statement: Creating polished instrumental music requires composition, rendering, and audio tooling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through MIDI composition, synthesis, transformation, rendering, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Guides original algorithmic composition with music21 notes, chords, instruments, tempo, dynamics, and structure.
Renders traditional MIDI arrangements to WAV or MP3 through FluidSynth and pydub.
Synthesizes electronic drums, bass, pads, and leads with genre-specific presets.
Extracts MIDI tempo, signatures, instruments, notes, timing, and velocity into structured JSON.
Transforms extracted music through transposition, tempo scaling, looping, extension, reversal, and instrument replacement.
Validates rendered audio for duration, format, clipping, silence, loudness, and channel properties.
limitations: The workflow creates instrumental music only and does not generate lyrics or vocals.
Rendering is offline and requires Python packages, FFmpeg, and FluidSynth for traditional instruments.
MIDI synthesis does not match the realism of professional sample libraries or studio recordings.
The included traditional renderer can delete matching MIDI or WAV files that share the selected output basename.

use_cases.title: Compose Music for Videos
use_cases.description: Create an original timed instrumental track with a defined mood, structure, duration, and downloadable audio output.

use_cases.title: Prototype Electronic Tracks
use_cases.description: Build house, techno, trance, ambient, or acid arrangements with synthesized drums, bass, pads, and leads.

use_cases.title: Study and Transform MIDI
use_cases.description: Inspect an existing MIDI composition, change its instrumentation or tempo, and render a new version.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Piano Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 30-second original piano theme in C major at 90 BPM. Use a clear melody, accompaniment, and gentle dynamics. Render an MP3.

prompt_templates.title: Arrange a Chamber Piece
prompt_templates.prompt: Compose a 60-second chamber piece for violin, cello, and piano. Use ABA form, natural ranges, expressive dynamics, and balanced voices. Export MIDI and MP3.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an Electronic Track
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a two-minute deep house track at 122 BPM. Use synthesized drums, sustained bass, evolving pads, and a sparse lead. Validate the final MP3.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze and Rework MIDI
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the provided MIDI structure. Summarize its tempo, key, tracks, and form. Transpose it up three semitones, replace piano with violin, then render MP3.

output_examples.input: Create a calm 45-second piano and violin piece in D major for a product video.
output_examples.output: A structured D-major composition with a gentle piano pattern, lyrical violin melody, dynamic shaping, MIDI source, and rendered MP3.

output_examples.input: Build a 90-second techno loop at 130 BPM with a strong kick and restrained lead.
output_examples.output: A techno arrangement using synthesized percussion, bass, pad, and lead layers, followed by loudness and clipping validation.

output_examples.input: Inspect this MIDI and create a slower version with acoustic guitar replacing piano.
output_examples.output: A concise structure summary, transformed timing and instrumentation, a revised MIDI file, and a rendered audio version.

best_practices: Define duration, tempo, key, genre, instruments, structure, and output format before composition begins.
Use unique output basenames and keep temporary MIDI, WAV, and final MP3 paths separate.
Validate duration, clipping, silence, channels, and loudness after every final render.
anti_patterns: Do not run the system installer without reviewing package changes and granting explicit permission.
Do not reuse an output basename when valuable MIDI or WAV files already exist beside it.
Do not expect vocals, real-time playback, or studio-sample realism from this MIDI-based workflow.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The documented workflows create MIDI, WAV, MP3, and structured JSON artifacts.

faq.question: Can this skill generate vocals or lyrics?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on instrumental composition and does not synthesize singing or spoken vocals.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing MIDI file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can extract structure, transform musical properties, change instruments, and render a revised version.

faq.question: Does it require additional software?
faq.answer: Yes. Traditional rendering requires Python dependencies, FFmpeg, FluidSynth, and an installed SoundFont.

faq.question: Which electronic genres have presets?
faq.answer: The bundled renderer includes deep house, techno, trance, ambient, acid house, and default presets.

faq.question: Are generated tracks studio quality?
faq.answer: No. The output is suitable for prototypes and general use, but professional sample libraries provide greater realism.
